react_result.final_narrative_text: The differential metabolomics signature is dominated by the **arachidonic acid metabolism** pathway (MUMM:arachidonic_acid_metabolism, KEGG:hsa00590). This pathway emerged as the top hit in the m/z-direct mummichog analysis (p=0.0034, 13/13 input lipid metabolites matched) and was independently validated in the KEGG-specific MetaboAnalystR PSEA (p=0.1062) and RaMP multi-DB ORA (REACT:R-HSA-211859 'Biological oxidations'). The driver metabolites are five polyoxygenated C20 lipid acids derived from arachidonic acid (AA): 8(S)-HPETE (C14823, CHEBI:34487), 16(R)-HETE (C14778, CHEBI:34162), 19(S)-HETE (C14749, CHEBI:34185), 11,12,15-THETA (C14782, CHEBI:34128), and thromboxane A2 (C02198, CHEBI:15627). 4-Hydroxyretinoic acid (C16677) additionally implicates the Vitamin A (retinol) metabolism pathway (MUMM rank 2, p=0.023), while S-adenosylmethionine (C00019) enriches a cluster of methylation pathways (Reactome nuclear signalling). Theophylline (C07130) and NaCl (C13563) are likely confounders/experimental artefacts — NaCl is biologically inert in signalling assays, and theophylline is a methylxanthine with a distinct pharmacology. No InChIKey conflicts were detected across the 10 input metabolites (10 unique block-14 identifiers, 0 structural disputes). Cross-paradigm consensus converges on **arachidonic acid as the principal substrate** whose oxidative metabolism is perturbed, consistent with treatment-induced COX/LOX pathway modulation.

  "narrative_text": "The treatment-versus-control comparison across ten metabolites converges on two dominant biological themes. The primary cross-paradigm signal is arachidonic acid metabolism, detected by m/z-direct analysis as the top mummichog hit (MUMM:arachidonic_acid_metabolism, p=0.0038, rank 1) and independently validated by KEGG PSEA at rank 4 (KEGG:hsa00590, p=0.1062). Five input eicosanoids — 8(S)-HPETE (C14823), 16(R)-HETE (C14778), 19(S)-HETE (C14749), thromboxane (C02198), and 11,12,15-THETA (C14782) — each map to this pathway in the mummichog metabolites_hit list. A second strongly supported signal, prostaglandin formation from arachidonate (MUMM:prostaglandin_formation_from_arachidonate, p=0.0145, rank 2), captures four of the same eicosanoids plus thromboxane. The eicosanoid series spans both the cyclooxygenase-derived thromboxane branch and the lipoxygenase-derived HPETE/HETE branch, indicating a broad enzymatic perturbation across the arachidonate cascade. Vitamin A metabolism emerges as a secondary validated signal: mummichog ranks it third (MUMM:vitamin_a_retinol_metabolism, p=0.0208) and MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA independently identifies the same biological process under hsa00830 (p=0.0421, rank 0), driven solely by 4-hydroxyretinoic acid (C16677). S-adenosylmethionine (C00019) enriches four methylation-related Reactome entries (Protein methylation, PKMTs methylate histone lysines, Defective TPMT causes TPMT deficiency, and Signaling by Nuclear Receptors), all sharing FDR=0.0015, with fold enrichment reaching 6755-fold for the single-carbon methylation entries.",

react_result.final_narrative_text: The treatment-versus-control comparison across ten metabolites converges on two dominant biological themes. The primary cross-paradigm signal is arachidonic acid metabolism, detected by m/z-direct analysis as the top mummichog hit (MUMM:arachidonic_acid_metabolism, p=0.0038, rank 1) and independently validated by KEGG PSEA at rank 4 (KEGG:hsa00590, p=0.1062). Five input eicosanoids — 8(S)-HPETE (C14823), 16(R)-HETE (C14778), 19(S)-HETE (C14749), thromboxane (C02198), and 11,12,15-THETA (C14782) — each map to this pathway in the mummichog metabolites_hit list. A second strongly supported signal, prostaglandin formation from arachidonate (MUMM:prostaglandin_formation_from_arachidonate, p=0.0145, rank 2), captures four of the same eicosanoids plus thromboxane. The eicosanoid series spans both the cyclooxygenase-derived thromboxane branch and the lipoxygenase-derived HPETE/HETE branch, indicating a broad enzymatic perturbation across the arachidonate cascade. Vitamin A metabolism emerges as a secondary validated signal: mummichog ranks it third (MUMM:vitamin_a_retinol_metabolism, p=0.0208) and MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA independently identifies the same biological process under hsa00830 (p=0.0421, rank 0), driven solely by 4-hydroxyretinoic acid (C16677). S-adenosylmethionine (C00019) enriches four methylation-related Reactome entries (Protein methylation, PKMTs methylate histone lysines, Defective TPMT causes TPMT deficiency, and Signaling by Nuclear Receptors), all sharing FDR=0.0015, with fold enrichment reaching 6755-fold for the single-carbon methylation entries.

final_react_result.final_narrative_text: Differential metabolomics analysis across three complementary enrichment paradigms identifies Arachidonic acid metabolism (MUMM:arachidonic_acid_metabolism) as the strongest m/z-direct hit, with all 13 input lipid species matching the pathway at p=0.0033. MetaboAnalystR PSEA independently validates Arachidonic acid metabolism (KEGG:hsa00590) at rank 4 (p=0.1062), confirming the signal across paradigms. The five driver lipid acids (8(S)-HPETE, 16(R)-HETE, 19(S)-HETE, 11,12,15-THETA, Thromboxane A2) are hydroxy- and hydroperoxy-eicosanoids derived from C20 polyunsaturated fatty acid oxidation. Prostaglandin formation from arachidonate (MUMM:prostaglandin_formation_from_arachidonate, rank 1, p=0.0128) captures thromboxane and the HPETE/HETE series, indicating concerted COX/LOX-branch perturbation. A secondary cross-validated signal is Vitamin A (retinol) metabolism (MUMM:vitamin_a_retinol_metabolism, rank 2, p=0.0192; KEGG:hsa00830, rank 0, p=0.0421), with 4-hydroxyretinoic acid as the sole input match in both tools. RaMP multi-DB ORA identifies Signaling by Nuclear Receptors (REACT:R-HSA-9006931, FDR=0.0015) as the top Reactome hit, driven by 4-hydroxyretinoic acid and S-adenosylmethionine; the latter independently enriches multiple methylation-related Reactome entries (Protein methylation, PKMTs methylate histone lysines). Six structurally distinct metabolites are confirmed by InChIKey reconciliation with zero block-14 conflicts, anchored by thromboxane A2 (InChIKey: RZWIIPASKMUIAC) and 11,12,15-THETA (InChIKey: PRMWQIVYOYCJQC).
